summary: Seventh-day Adventist physician John Harvey Kellogg ran the Battle Creek Sanitarium in Michigan from 1876, promoting enemas and fad cures, torturing and genitally mutilating children to stop masturbation, and campaigning for eugenics.

evidence.note: Adventism grows out of the Great Disappointment; Ellen White's prophetic role begins
family conversion and his birth in February 1852
church opens its own hydropathy medical school and sends him there
made superintendent and renames the institute the Battle Creek Sanitarium
auto-intoxication theory and high-volume enema machine
electrified catheter treatment for masturbating patients
his warning signs of masturbation overlap with signs of child sexual abuse
genital surgery on girls and circumcision without anaesthetic as punishment
disfellowshipped in 1907, then embraces eugenics as race betterment
eugenics conferences and Michigan forced sterilization law
fourth conference cancelled after Pearl Harbor; dies in Battle Creek

notes: Death year 1943 from general knowledge (transcript gives only December). covered_span starts at the 1844 founding of Adventism; the Millerite preaching from 1831 is treated as background. Adventism is a mainstream denomination today but the story treats its early form as an apocalyptic sect, hence cults-new-religions; organized-religion is the alternative. Transcript says he was 26 at the superintendency; 1876 used.
